chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah: 'Surely Allah commands you to make over trusts to their owners and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent,' and Abu Ja'far al-Baqir said:

The order of Allah in this verse concerns the imamate. Each imam of us has to deliver the imamate to the next imam coming after him. He does not have to hide it from him. Do you not hear Allah saying: (and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent)? It is the rulers. Do you not see that Allah has addressed the rulers with this verse?

key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: The trusts, here interpreted as the Imamate
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: The Imam, specifically referring to the divinely appointed leader in Shia theology
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةَ: The Imamate, the office or authority of the Imam
key_terms.الْحُكَّامُ: The rulers, identified here as the Imams
key_terms.بَيْنَ النَّاسِ: Between the people, referring to the community of believers

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir interpret the 'trusts' mentioned in Surah An-Nisa verse 58?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates that the 'trust' (amanah) in Surah An-Nisa 4:58 specifically denotes the Imamate, establishing a divine mandate for each Imam to transfer authority to his designated successor without omission. By linking the term 'al-hukkam' (rulers/judges) in the verse to the Imams, the text underscores their dual role as both political leaders and infallible judges, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of explicit designation (nass) for leadership continuity.
